solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What can calm taken by mouth mostly? Sleeping draught perhaps

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sop is something given to pacify or appease
an orifice is an opening such as the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which oral remedy might soothe them, and settles on a sleeping draught.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; everything after it is the definition. 'Mostly' trims only the final letter of the mouth word.
explanation.definitionFit: A soporific is a noun as well as an adjective: any drug or drink that induces sleep, of which a sleeping draught is one example.

clue.text: Places erected including European institute

indicators.note: in a down clue, something erected is stood upright, so its letters read from bottom to top
to include something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: to place something is to put it
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Buildings are put up to house a European institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institute' looks like a noun completing the phrase, but it is the verb, meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute a scheme or body is to establish or found it, which is exactly what setting something up means.

clue.text: What child may do with penny toy

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
a baby's rattle is a toy

explanation.surface: A child is handed a cheap toy and wonders what to do with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something a child does with a penny toy; in fact 'What child may do' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children chatter away in a babbling, childish manner, and that talking is the verb in question.

clue.text: Judiciously restrict the consumption of supporter

blocks.note: to ration food is to limit how much is eaten
an ally supports you

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly cuts down on what a backer consumes.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase in the middle reads as an instruction about eating, but it is a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To act judiciously is to act with sound judgement, sensibly and by reason, so the adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Raid gold in possession of fairy

indicators.note: whatever is held in someone's possession is inside their grasp, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
fay is an old literary word for a fairy

explanation.surface: A raid seizes gold that a fairy was hoarding.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry and is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden attack or incursion into enemy territory, often to seize plunder, which is a raid.

clue.text: Entrust to support group making decisions

blocks.note: to commit something to someone is to entrust it
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Someone hands a matter over to a decision-making body for backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' is not a verb here: it is the peg a golfer rests the ball on.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee is a body of people appointed to deliberate and reach conclusions on some matter.

clue.text: Lie about strength of character

blocks.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone tells untruths about another person's moral backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a preposition linking the halves, but it supplies RE, the Latin-derived 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral fibre is toughness and resolve of personality, so the word alone can mean inner strength.

clue.text: First-rate tarts turned out light

indicators.note: something turned is faced the other way, so its letters run backwards
what is out has been excluded, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Excellent pastries have come out light and airy.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters are a backwards run sitting right in the middle of the hyphenated word; 'turned out' looks like a baking phrase but gives two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a candle or fuse is to set fire to it, and a fire also gives light; the verb or noun both fit.

clue.text: “British” and “English” align badly in a foreign tongue

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: British and English speakers struggle to line up their words when using another language.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest two words being discussed; they are simply the letters B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal, a tongue foreign to Britain.

clue.text: Work in copper, perhaps making a bolt?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
copper is an example of a chemical element

explanation.surface: A metalworker hammering copper might be fashioning a bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a policeman or a metal to work; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a class. 'Bolt' is not hardware but running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run away secretly to marry are said to make a bolt for it, which is what eloping is.

clue.text: What makes round brown circle in sampler

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: O is shaped like a circle
someone who samples food is a taster

explanation.surface: Something that turns a round object brown leaves a ring inside a piece of embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'round' here is a round of toast, a slice of bread; a sampler is also a piece of embroidery, but here it is someone who tries food.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen appliance browns slices of bread, and a single slice of toast is called a round.

clue.text: Horse and knight advance in battle

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
N is the chess notation for a knight
to go forward is to advance

explanation.surface: Cavalry, horse and rider, push forward during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Marengo was also the name of Napoleon's horse, so 'Horse' tempts as the definition; the battle is the one he won in 1800.
explanation.definitionFit: Marengo is the site in northern Italy where Napoleon defeated the Austrians in 1800, a famous battle.

clue.text: Copy Martin, perhaps, as a name from an earlier generation

definitions.text: a name from an earlier generation

indicators.note: perhaps admits other possibilities, so the letters may be arranged another way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone might imitate a man called Martin by taking on an old family name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' after a name usually signals an example; here it signals rearranging the two preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: A patronymic is a name derived from a father or ancestor, such as Johnson from John.

clue.text: Reported murderer for punishment

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A killer is said to have been sentenced to punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Cain, the first murderer in the Bible, is pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane is a stick formerly used to beat pupils, and the word stands for that corporal punishment itself.

clue.text: Lawyer’s dull discourse upset court

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: prose can mean dull, commonplace talk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A barrister's boring speech has annoyed the judge and jury.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as a possessive, but it stands for 'is' and links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor is the lawyer who conducts the case against a defendant in a criminal trial.

clue.text: Type of work aspiration for Cockney artist

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the aitch at the start of words

blocks.note: an aspiration is a hope
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An East End painter hopes to produce a particular kind of work.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent, which drops the H. 'Aspiration' also means an H sound, a neat hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a genre of musical work, and it is also the plural of opus, meaning works.

clue.text: Children start well

blocks.note: the off is the start of a race
a spring is a source of water, a well

explanation.surface: Kids get off to a good beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an adverb but is the noun for a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's offspring are their sons and daughters, their descendants.

clue.text: Shade regularly keeps spinning endlessly in grave

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter
without an end means the last letter goes
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters
spinning is turning

explanation.surface: A ghost keeps whirling about in its tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' tempts as a ghost or a colour, and 'grave' as a tomb; the first gives letters and the second is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, sombre, serious temperament, supposedly under the influence of the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Sight pâté being prepared for this dish

indicators.note: food being prepared is chopped and mixed, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, accent dropped

explanation.surface: A cook eyes the pâté being got ready as part of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This dish' refers back to the answer itself, a pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is the long thin Italian pasta and also the meal made from it.

clue.text: Series of shots initially are downed easily after a lot of pasta

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the tail is cut
initially means at the start, so only first letters are kept

blocks.note: fusilli is spiral-shaped pasta
the opening letters of three words

explanation.surface: After plenty of pasta, a few rounds of drinks slip down easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' sounds like drinks in this pasta-and-drink scene, but they are gunshots. FUSILLI loses its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a rapid burst of gunfire from many weapons, a series of shots in quick succession.

clue.text: Surround with small dam

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
in animal breeding a dam is the female parent

explanation.surface: Engineers enclose water with a small dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' suggests a barrier on a river, but in animal breeding it means the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover or envelop it completely, so it can mean enclose on all sides.

clue.text: Special constable not allowed to reconnoitre

blocks.note: SC is the abbreviation for a special constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain
in games, a shot that is out is not allowed

explanation.surface: A volunteer police officer is barred from surveying the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer officer in British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To scout an area is to explore it to gather information, which is the military sense of reconnoitring.

clue.text: Local drink has never to be tipped in flute

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so without them only the inner letters stay

blocks.note: inner letters of the word
inner letters of the word
inner letter of the word

explanation.surface: At the pub, a drink must never be poured into a champagne glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' suggests pouring or reversing; here it means having tips, so each of the first three words loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes, a simple kind of flute.

clue.text: Shut up about old farm worker

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: to pen an animal is to shut it up
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone tells an elderly labourer to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as a rude command to be silent, but it means to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: A peon is a Latin American labourer, especially one working on a farm or estate for low pay.

clue.text: Bird, one very loud, at first calling hidden in cut hay

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters only
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
the opening letters of both words
chaff is chopped hay or straw used as fodder

explanation.surface: A single loud bird's call rings out, unseen, from a hayfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal but only lends its first letter, and the whole group slips in after the second letter of the hay word. The chiffchaff is a small European warbler named for its two-note song.
explanation.definitionFit: The chiffchaff is a small olive-green warbler common in Europe, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Down with viral infection following start of freeze

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: flu is influenza, a viral infection
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone is laid low by a virus after the cold weather sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like feeling low, and 'following' looks like a link word, but one is the definition and the other gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is soft, fine feathers or fuzz, and fluff is the same kind of light fluffy material.

clue.text: Sweet — for instance doughy pudding — not finished up

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its ending, so the last letter goes
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'
duff is a British steamed or boiled flour pudding, as in plum duff

explanation.surface: A dessert such as a heavy pudding has been left half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Duff is a stodgy British pudding made from flour, as in plum duff; it loses its last letter before the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fudge is a soft confection made from sugar, butter and milk, one kind of sweet or candy.

clue.text: Priest born in Lincoln?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: b is the abbreviation for born
Abe, short for Abraham, is a name, as with President Lincoln

explanation.surface: A clergyman is said to hail from the English city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is a cathedral city in England, but the question mark signals Abraham Lincoln, known as Abe.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French clergyman or abbot, so the word is a title for a priest.

clue.text: Occupy hotel, soon to go outside

indicators.note: to go outside something is to wrap around it, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in a bit means soon

explanation.surface: Guests take over a hotel and will shortly head out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about leaving; the outside refers to where a letter-group sits.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in it, which is to occupy it as a resident.

clue.text: Still to be evaluated back on Manchester United ground

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter
something ground is crushed up, so its letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: the final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new player at Old Trafford has yet to be assessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' tempts as a football stadium, but it is the past participle of grind. Manchester United is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untried has not yet been tested or put to trial, so it remains to be judged.

clue.text: Druidic council axing hollow dead shrub

indicators.note: a hollow thing has lost its insides, leaving just the outside letters
to axe something is to cut it away, so letters are removed

blocks.note: a gorsedd is an assembly of Welsh bards and druids
just the outer letters

explanation.surface: A council of druids clears away a dried-up bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gorsedd is the Welsh bardic assembly behind the Eisteddfod; take off its closing DD and a common plant appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, also called furze, is a spiny evergreen bush with yellow flowers found on heathland.

clue.text: Bug within pelt one put away

blocks.note: within means in
an animal's pelt is its fur
I is the Roman numeral one
to put food away is to eat it

explanation.surface: An insect living in an animal's coat gets eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' wants to be an insect and 'within' a container signal, but 'Bug' is the verb meaning annoy and 'within' simply gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is informally to irritate or anger them, so the verbs are synonyms in the sense of annoy.
